key_insight: A verified knowledge-based algorithm for pancreatic cancer staging outperformed a retrieval-augmented LLM and unaided radiologists on guideline-based staging tasks.
clinical_relevance: For tasks governed by explicit rules, a validated algorithm may improve staging accuracy while avoiding the time penalty seen with LLM assistance.
method: Implemented a web-based KBA covering TNM, stage, and resectability classifications from current Japanese guidelines.
Exhaustively checked correctness across all possible inputs.
Compared six non-board-certified radiologists across 12 simulated cases under unassisted, LLM-assisted, and KBA-assisted conditions.
evidence_signal: In the simulated comparison, accuracy was 98.6% with KBA versus 81.9% unassisted and 80.6% with LLM assistance, while mean staging time was lowest with KBA (196.2 s) and highest with LLM (401.9 s).
watch_item: This was a small preliminary simulation study, so real-world performance, usability, and generalizability still need confirmation.
paper_title: Algorithmic implementation of pancreatic cancer staging guidelines: comparison with a retrieval-augmented large language model
